sections.title: 3. Introduction
sections.body:
### 3.1 Purpose
The purpose of this Business Requirements Document (BRD) is to define the business needs, objectives, and scope for the development of a comprehensive Human Resources Management System (HRMS). This document serves as the foundational reference for stakeholders, project managers, and technical teams to align on the functional and non-functional requirements of the system.

### 3.2 Project Background
The organization requires a centralized, full-stack web and mobile application to manage end-to-end HR processes. Currently, HR operations may be fragmented or manual, leading to inefficiencies in tracking employee data, payroll, recruitment, and performance. The proposed HRMS will consolidate these functions into a single, secure, and scalable platform.

### 3.3 Business Problem
The lack of an integrated HR system results in data silos, manual errors in payroll and attendance, slow recruitment cycles, and limited visibility into workforce analytics. There is a critical need for a system that automates workflows, ensures compliance with banking industry standards (PCI-DSS, SOX, AML/KYC, ISO 27001), and provides real-time insights for decision-making.

### 3.4 Business Objectives
| ID | Objective | Success Measure |
|---|---|---|
| BO-01 | Centralize HR data management | 100% of employee master data migrated and accessible via single pane of glass |
| BO-02 | Automate payroll and attendance | Reduction of manual payroll processing time by 80% |
| BO-03 | Streamline recruitment process | Reduction of time-to-hire by 30% |
| BO-04 | Ensure regulatory compliance | Zero critical compliance violations in annual audit |
| BO-05 | Enhance employee self-service | 90% of routine HR queries resolved via self-service portal |

### 3.5 Expected Business Benefits
- Improved operational efficiency through automation of repetitive HR tasks.
- Enhanced data accuracy and integrity in payroll and employee records.
- Better employee experience through mobile access and self-service capabilities.
- Real-time analytics for strategic workforce planning.
- Stronger security and compliance posture aligned with banking industry standards.

sections.title: 4. Scope
sections.body:
### 4.1 In Scope
The project includes the development of a full-stack HRMS with the following modules:
- Secure Authentication and Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
- Employee Master Data Management (Departments, Designations, Branches)
- Onboarding and Offboarding Workflows
- Attendance, Shift, and Roster Management
- Leave and Holiday Management
- Payroll, Salary Structures, and Deductions
- Recruitment and Applicant Tracking System (ATS)
- Performance Management and Appraisals
- Training and Learning Management
- Asset Management
- Expense and Reimbursement Management
- Notifications and Communication (Email, SMS, Push)
- Dashboards and Reporting
- API Integrations and Mobile Applications (Android, iOS)

### 4.2 Out of Scope
- Payroll tax filing with government authorities (integration only, not submission)
- Biometric hardware integration (unless specified in future phases)
- Third-party benefits administration (integration only)
- Legacy system data migration beyond the defined master data entities

### 4.3 System Boundaries
The HRMS will operate as a centralized backend API with a relational database, file storage, and notification services. It will integrate with external systems for email, SMS, and calendar services. The system will support web, Android, and iOS clients. All data processing will occur within the organization's secure infrastructure, adhering to ISO 27001 and PCI-DSS standards.

sections.title: 7. Business Process Overview
sections.body:
### 7.1 AS-IS Process
Currently, HR processes are managed through disparate tools and manual spreadsheets. Employee data is stored in multiple locations, leading to inconsistencies. Payroll is processed manually, increasing the risk of errors. Recruitment is tracked via email and basic spreadsheets, lacking visibility into candidate pipelines. Performance reviews are conducted annually with limited feedback mechanisms.

### 7.2 TO-BE Process
The TO-BE process involves a centralized HRMS that automates end-to-end HR workflows. Employee data is maintained in a single source of truth. Payroll is processed automatically based on attendance and leave data. Recruitment is managed through an integrated ATS with real-time pipeline tracking. Performance management is continuous with regular feedback and appraisals.

### 7.3 Process Flow Narrative Description
The core business process flow is: Recruitment → Candidate Selection → Offer → Joining → Onboarding → Employee → Attendance/Leave → Payroll → Performance → Promotion/Transfer → Offboarding/Exit. Each stage involves configurable approval chains for HR, managers, finance, and admins. The system supports bulk import/export, PDF generation, and audit logs for all transactions.

sections.title: 9. Functional Requirements
sections.body:
### Module: Authentication and RBAC
- **Description**: Secure login with JWT/session management, password policies, and MFA-ready architecture.
- **Preconditions**: User account exists and is active.
- **Input**: Username, password, MFA token (if enabled).
- **Processing**: Validate credentials, generate JWT token, enforce RBAC.
- **Output**: Authenticated session with role-specific access.
- **Business Rules**: Passwords must meet complexity requirements; sessions expire after 30 minutes of inactivity.
- **Acceptance Criteria**: Given a valid user, when they log in with correct credentials, then they are granted access based on their role.

### Module: Employee Master Data
- **Description**: Manage employee profiles, departments, designations, and branches.
- **Preconditions**: User has HR/Admin or Super Admin role.
- **Input**: Employee details (name, ID, department, designation, branch).
- **Processing**: Validate data, save to database, log audit trail.
- **Output**: Updated employee record.
- **Business Rules**: Employee ID must be unique; department and designation must exist in master data.
- **Acceptance Criteria**: Given an HR admin, when they create a new employee, then the employee record is saved and visible in the employee list.

### Module: Payroll
- **Description**: Process payroll based on attendance, leave, and salary structures.
- **Preconditions**: Attendance and leave data are finalized for the period.
- **Input**: Salary structure, attendance data, deductions.
- **Processing**: Calculate gross pay, deductions, and net pay; generate payslips.
- **Output**: Payroll report and PDF payslips.
- **Business Rules**: Payroll must be atomic; any error in calculation must roll back the transaction.
- **Acceptance Criteria**: Given a finance user, when they process payroll for a month, then payslips are generated and accessible to employees.

sections.title: 10. Non-Functional Requirements
sections.body:
### 10.1 Performance
- The system must support 10,000 concurrent users with a response time of less than 2 seconds for standard queries.
- Payroll processing for 5,000 employees must complete within 10 minutes.

### 10.2 Security
- Comply with PCI-DSS, SOX, AML/KYC, and ISO 27001 standards.
- Implement RBAC, JWT/session management, password policies, and MFA-ready architecture.
- Ensure data privacy and audit trails for all sensitive operations.

### 10.3 Availability
- The system must achieve 99.99% uptime, with planned maintenance windows scheduled during off-peak hours.

### 10.4 Scalability
- The system must scale horizontally to support up to 50,000 employees without performance degradation.

### 10.5 Usability
- The UI must be modern, responsive, and accessible on web, Android, and iOS devices.
- Key tasks (e.g., leave request, payslip download) must be completable in no more than 3 clicks.

### 10.6 Maintainability
- The system must be API-driven, well-documented, and modular to facilitate future enhancements.
- Audit logs and activity history must be immutable and retained for at least 7 years per SOX requirements.

### 10.7 Compatibility
- The system must support the latest versions of Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge browsers.
- Mobile apps must support Android 10+ and iOS 14+.

sections.title: 11. Business Rules
table: Each employee must have a unique identifier across the system
Payroll transactions must be atomic; any failure must roll back the entire process
Audit logs must be immutable and retained for at least 7 years
Users can only access modules and data permitted by their role
Leave requests must follow the configured approval chain (e.g., Manager → HR)

sections.title: 12. Data Requirements
sections.body:
### 12.1 Data Entities List
- Employee
- Department
- Designation
- Branch
- Attendance
- Leave Request
- Payroll Record
- Job Posting
- Candidate
- Performance Review

### 12.2 Data Fields
| Entity | Field | Data Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Employee | Employee ID | String | Yes | Unique identifier for the employee |
| Employee | Name | String | Yes | Full name of the employee |
| Employee | Department ID | String | Yes | Foreign key to Department |
| Attendance | Date | Date | Yes | Date of attendance |
| Attendance | Status | Enum | Yes | Present, Absent, Leave |
| Payroll Record | Employee ID | String | Yes | Foreign key to Employee |
| Payroll Record | Gross Pay | Decimal | Yes | Total gross pay |
| Payroll Record | Net Pay | Decimal | Yes | Total net pay after deductions |

### 12.3 Data Validation
- Employee ID must be unique and non-editable after creation.
- Attendance status must be one of the predefined enum values.
- Payroll calculations must validate against salary structures.

### 12.4 Data Retention
- Employee master data: Retained for the duration of employment + 7 years.
- Payroll records: Retained for 7 years per SOX.
- Audit logs: Retained for 7 years per SOX.

sections.title: 14. Interface Requirements
sections.body:
### 14.1 User Interface
- Modern, responsive UI for web, Android, and iOS.
- Dashboards with HR analytics (headcount, attendance, leave utilization, attrition, etc.).
- Search, filters, sorting, and pagination for all lists.
- Bulk import/export via Excel/CSV.

### 14.2 API Interface
- Centralized backend API with RESTful endpoints.
- JWT-based authentication for API access.
- Rate limiting and API authorization for security.

### 14.3 Hardware Interface
- No specific hardware requirements beyond standard servers and storage.
- Mobile devices must support standard web and native app capabilities.

sections.title: 15. Security Requirements
table: Encrypt data at rest and in transit

sections.title: 18. Assumptions and Dependencies
sections.body:
### Assumptions
- The organization has a stable internet connection for cloud-based services.
- Employees have access to mobile devices for the mobile app.
- Existing employee data is clean and can be migrated to the new system.

### Dependencies
- Integration with external email and SMS services.
- Availability of a secure file storage service.
- Completion of data migration before go-live.

sections.body:

- **Regulatory**: Must comply with PCI-DSS, SOX, AML/KYC, and ISO 27001.

- **Infrastructure**: Must support 99.99% uptime and horizontal scaling.

sections.title: 20. Risks
table: Perform multiple test migrations and validate data integrity
Conduct regular security audits and penetration testing

sections.title: 21. Acceptance Criteria
sections.body:
The system will be accepted when:
- All functional requirements (BR-001 to BR-008) are implemented and tested.
- All non-functional requirements (performance, security, availability) are met.
- Data migration is completed with 100% accuracy.
- User acceptance testing (UAT) is passed by all stakeholder groups.
- Security audit confirms compliance with PCI-DSS, SOX, AML/KYC, and ISO 27001.

HR Management System 
 
Build a complete HR Management System (HRMS) as a full-stack web and mobile 
application with role-based access for Super Admin, HR/Admin, Manager, Recruiter, 
Employee, and Finance/Payroll users. The system should include **secure authentication, 
role and permission management, employee master data, departments, designations, branches, 
employee onboarding/offboarding, employee profiles, document management, attendance, 
shift and roster management, leave and holiday management, work-from-home/remote-work 
requests, regularization, timesheets, payroll, salary structures, deductions, bonuses, 
reimbursements, payslips, tax/statutory information, recruitment and applicant tracking, job 
postings, candidate pipeline, interviews, offers, joining management, performance 
management, goals/KPIs, appraisals, feedback, training and learning, asset management, 
employee grievances, announcements, notifications, company policies, HR letters/certificates, 
expense management, travel requests, approval workflows, surveys, employee self-service, 
manager self-service, and comprehensive dashboards and reports. Include search, filters, 
sorting, pagination, bulk import/export, Excel/CSV upload, PDF generation, audit logs, 
activity history, configurable workflows, email/SMS/push notifications, reminders, 
calendar integration, and API integrations. The dashboard should provide HR analytics 
such as headcount, attendance, leave utilization, attrition, recruitment status, payroll 
summaries, department statistics, performance, pending approvals, and upcoming events. 
The project should have a modern responsive UI for Web, Android, and iOS, with a 
centralized backend API, relational database, file/document storage, notification service, 
background jobs, logging, monitoring, validation, encryption, backups, and strong security 
including RBAC, JWT/session management, password policies, MFA-ready architecture, 
API authorization, data privacy, audit trails, and secure document access. Define 
complete workflows such as Recruitment → Candidate Selection → Offer → Joining → 
Onboarding → Employee → Attendance/Leave → Payroll → Performance → 
Promotion/Transfer → Offboarding/Exit, with configurable approval chains for HR, 
managers, finance, and admins. Include master-data configuration, organization settings, 
financial/payroll settings, notification templates, workflow configuration, reports, audit logs, 
and system administration. The final system should be production-ready, scalable, API-
driven, well-documented, tested, and include BRD, SRS, database schema/ERD, API 
documentation, RTM, UI/UX specifications, user stories with acceptance criteria, test 
cases, deployment documentation, and complete role-wise functional requirements.
